summary: Passing the fig tree withered from the roots, Jesus tells His amazed disciples to have faith in God, to pray believing, and to forgive when they pray.
key_insight: Peter wanted to talk about the dead tree. Jesus turned the talk to prayer, and He ended with forgiveness: “whenever you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive him.” Disciples who had just seen a curse take effect at His word were not to pray with grudges.
story: The next morning, as they passed by on the road from Bethany, the disciples saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. {Mk} Peter remembered and said to Jesus, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which You cursed has withered away.” {Mk} The disciples marveled, “How did the fig tree wither away so soon?” {Mt}

Jesus answered, “Have faith in God.” {Mk} Then He said, “Assuredly, I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but also if you say to this mountain, ‘Be removed and be cast into the sea,’ it will be done.” {Mt}
“Therefore I say to you, whatever things you ask when you pray, believe that you receive them, and you will have them.” {Mk}

Then He added, “And whenever you stand praying, if you have anything against anyone, forgive him, that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your trespasses.” {Mk}
differences: Matthew tells the cursing and the withering in one scene, so the disciples marvel right away (see event 133). Mark tells of the withered tree the next morning.
In Mark, Peter speaks for the group: “Rabbi, look!” In Matthew, the disciples marvel together and ask how it happened “so soon.”
Only Mark records “Have faith in God” and the command to forgive when praying, with its warning: “if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your trespasses.”
Only Matthew adds “you will not only do what was done to the fig tree.”

scene.label: “This mountain”
scene.text: Jesus spoke on the road over the Mount of Olives. From that ridge the Temple Mount stands in view to the west, and on a clear day the Dead Sea can be seen far below to the east. “This mountain” may be the one under their feet, or the temple hill they were walking toward; Jesus does not say.

scene.label: Dried up from the roots
scene.text: Mark’s phrase means the tree was dead through and through, not merely wilting. Hosea used the same picture of judgment on Israel: “Their root is dried up; They shall bear no fruit” (Hosea 9:16).

scene.label: Standing to pray
scene.text: Jews usually stood to pray, as Hannah did at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1:26) and the Pharisee and the tax collector did in the temple (Luke 18:11, 13). Jesus pictures a disciple already on his feet in prayer when a grudge comes to mind.

scene.label: Prayer and forgiveness
scene.text: Jesus had already tied the two together in the prayer He taught: “And forgive us our debts, As we forgive our debtors” (Matthew 6:12). Here He ties forgiveness to one of His boldest promises about prayer.

scene.label: Verse 26
scene.text: The NKJV includes Mark 11:26 and notes that some manuscripts do not have it. Jesus gives the same teaching in almost the same words in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 6:15), so the teaching does not rest on this verse alone.

witnesses.matthew: Finishes the fig tree in one scene, so the disciples’ amazement follows the curse directly. His emphasis falls on faith that does not doubt and on prayer offered “believing” (21:22).
witnesses.mark: Gives Peter’s voice, the discovery the next morning and the detail “dried up from the roots.” Only Mark adds the call to forgive, so faith toward God and mercy toward others stand side by side.

seeing.reveals: Jesus does not explain the miracle or show it off. He points beyond it to God: the power behind His word is the Father’s, and He invites His disciples to rely on that same Father in prayer.
seeing.living: Jesus joins two things we tend to keep apart: bold faith and a forgiving heart. Bring God the mountain you cannot move, and believe He hears. But before you ask, let go of the grudge; He says the two belong together.
seeing.ponder: When you stand to pray, whose name comes to mind that you have not yet forgiven?

preaching.big_idea: Faith in God can move mountains, and forgiveness keeps the way of prayer open.
preaching.watch_for: Jesus’ answer begins, “Have faith in God” (v. 22). The promise rests on God, not on the strength of the one praying. And it sits between two settings: a tree judged for having no fruit, and a heart told to forgive.
